title: Janus Nanoporous Metal–Phenolic Nanosheet Membranes for Highly Efficient Osmotic Energy Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT Osmotic energy, harvested by reverse electrodialysis, is a huge and promising renewable power source. However, the implementation still remains a longstanding bottleneck due to the lack of high‐efficiency membranes with both remarkable ionic conductivity and high permselectivity. Here, we report a new membrane constructed by Janus nanoporous metal–phenolic nanosheets (Janus MPNs), which overcomes the intrinsic trade‐off between ion permeability and selectivity. The Janus MPNs prepared via a facile interface‐induced coordination assembly strategy feature an asymmetric bilayer architecture comprising a microporous domain containing ∼0.96 nm pores and a mesoporous domain containing ∼9.4 nm pores, with each domain approximately 10 nm thick. The assembled Janus MPNs membrane integrates interlayer 2D nanofluidic pathways with ordered intralayer 1D nanochannels, enabling ultrafast ion transport rates approximately 21 times those of membranes relying solely on interlamellar transport. More importantly, the intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores and abundant negative surface charges within the metal–phenolic framework enable high cation selectivity, yielding a cation transference number ( t + ) of ∼0.936. When applied in reverse electrodialysis, the Janus MPNs membrane delivers a power density of 22.1 W m −2 under a simulated sea/river salinity gradient, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art two dimensional (2D)‐material‐based membranes. This work establishes new scaffolds for membrane technology and osmotic energy harvesting.

title: A Biodegradable Metal–Organic Framework/Oligomer Composite for Sustainable Gold Recovery and Circular Water Management
abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of artificial intelligence and digital technologies is generating unprecedented e-waste streams rich in secondary gold resources, yet sustainable recovery strategies remain scarce. Here, we report a bioderived, environmentally degradable metal–organic framework (MOF)/oligomer composite (SU-102/pGSH) constructed via host–guest self-assembly of glutathione (GSH) within a Zr-ellagate framework. The composite integrates abundant electron-rich functional groups into a robust porous architecture, achieving a remarkable gold uptake capacity of 4385 mg·g–1, the highest reported for MOF-based adsorbents. It also exhibits outstanding selectivity in complex e-waste leachates. Mechanistic investigations reveal synergistic coordination with abundant electron-rich groups, followed by electron-transfer reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). Importantly, the spent adsorbent could degrade into benign mineral phases and natural metabolites with negligible phytotoxicity, ensuring a safe end-of-life pathway. Preliminary techno-economic analysis indicates favorable economic potential for practical implementation. By integrating efficient gold recovery with sustainable material design and end-of-life management, this work provides a viable strategy for circular water treatment.

title: Interfacial Kinetic Control Enables Regulated Growth of Functional Metal–Phenolic Network Films
abstract: Abstract Metal–phenolic network (MPN) films are of widespread interest because of their potential application in biotechnology, catalysis, and the environment. Their formation typically involves the supramolecular assembly of phenolic ligands and metal ions from solution onto a solid substrate. Such assembly has been conducted exclusively from a single-phase solution, thus limiting spatiotemporal control over coordination and/or the range of precursors that can be used, and thereby restricting the compositional and structural diversity, as well as functionality, of MPN films. Herein, we report a liquid–liquid interfacial assembly (LLIA) approach, which leverages two immiscible phases, to prepare functional MPN films with specific properties. LLIA enables both the kinetic regulation of film growth (a key parameter in designing films with desired properties) and the use of a broader range of building blocks. The assembled MPN films exhibit controlled thickness (∼30–500 nm) and stiffness (∼2–12 GPa) and distinct structural properties (e.g., crystallinity) relative to other methods, which contribute to their conductivity and molecular selectivity (e.g., H2/CO2 separation performance). Functional MPN films with wettability, conductivity, antibacterial, or fluorescence properties are assembled by integrating various functional components (e.g., polymers, nanoparticles, and dyes), as well as inorganic and metal–organic framework films.

title: Role of Intermolecular Association in Monolayer-Level Assembly and Morphogenesis of Conjugated Polymers at the Air–Water Interface
abstract: Abstract How molecular architecture is translated through intermolecular association into film structure and mechanical behavior remains a central question in conjugated-polymer self-assembly. Here, we compare two luminescent polymers with distinct backbone and side-chain structures: poly(9,9-di-n-octylfluorenyl-2,7-diyl) (PFO) and poly(2,5-di(3′,7′-dimethyloctyl)phenylene-1,4-ethynylene) (PPE). Langmuir–Blodgett processing provides a controlled two-dimensional environment at the air–water interface, while the intrinsic fluorescence of both polymers allows interfacial organization to be followed from the earliest stages of spreading. PFO rapidly forms discrete domains. PPE instead develops a laterally interconnected network. Molecular dynamics simulations relate these morphologies to different modes of intermolecular association. In PFO, fluorene units associate more locally, favoring compact aggregation. PPE instead forms more spatially distributed contacts along the phenylene–ethynylene backbone. This distinction persists during mechanical deformation. Compression brings pre-existing PFO domains into contact, but decompression rapidly fragments the film. PPE remains laterally connected and undergoes extensive expansion. Deformation is accommodated predominantly through the ethynylene linkages of the conjugated backbone. Beyond the monolayer stability limit, both polymers develop anisotropic semicrystalline structures. PFO forms isolated needle-like domains, whereas PPE develops an interconnected fibrillar network. The results thus establish a hierarchical link between local intermolecular association and the subsequent evolution of monolayer structure and mechanical behavior. This relationship remains reflected in the ordered structures formed after monolayer collapse and provides a basis for designing ultrathin conjugated-polymer films with controlled lateral connectivity and anisotropic organization.

title: Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Framework-Confined Carbon Dots toward Efficient Red Room-Temperature Phosphorescence via Resonance Energy Transfer
abstract: Abstract Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials are promising for information encryption and anticounterfeiting. However, realizing long-wavelength RTP of carbon dots (CDs) is challenging owing to unstable triplet states and strong nonradiative decay. Herein, we construct a hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF) through molecular self-assembly and realize the in situ generation of CDs within the HOF matrix. By further incorporating Rhodamine B (RhB) into the HOF, a donor–acceptor resonance energy transfer (RET) system is established, enabling efficient red RTP emission. In this system, the HOF matrix provides a confined environment for the CDs and RhB. Meanwhile, the hydrogen-bonded network restricts excited-state molecular motions and suppresses nonradiative relaxation. The optimized CDs-RhB@HOF composite exhibits outstanding red phosphorescence centered at 600 nm, achieving a high PLQY of 34.20% (versus 0.71% for CDs@HOF) and a prolonged lifetime of 458 ms. The composite material has been successfully applied to multilevel anticounterfeiting encryption.

title: Joule Heating Induced Structural Evolution of Ordered Mesoporous Mg-Al Spinel-Related Oxides
abstract: Coupling block copolymer self-assembly with ultrafast Joule heating enables second-scale crystallization of ordered mesoporous oxides while preserving long-range mesoscopic order. Using this strategy, we synthesize long-range ordered mesoporous magnesium-aluminum oxide frameworks at low magnesium contents exhibiting defect spinel-related nanocrystalline structures. Ex situ isothermal holds at 1000 to 1155 °C reveal rapid crystallite enlargement followed by a plateau in apparent crystallite size. In pure γ-alumina, this early saturation, together with retention of the ordered mesostructure, is consistent with geometrically constrained crystallite growth. Magnesium incorporation enables further crystallite enlargement before saturation, yielding larger defect-spinel-related domains while retaining long-range mesoscopic order. We further demonstrate the incorporation of in situ crystallized platinum nanoparticles within the ordered magnesium-aluminum oxide framework and their activity for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation at 350 °C. These results demonstrate that ultrafast Joule heating can access distinct crystallization trajectories in compositionally modified mesoporous oxides that are precluded by mesostructural collapse during conventional furnace heating.

title: Core–Shell Co@v‐CoO x /C Electrocatalysts With Balanced Intermediate Adsorption for High‐Performance Rechargeable Zinc–Air Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Vacancy engineering offers an effective route to tailoring Co‐based oxygen electrocatalysts, yet vacancy‐rich sites can also intensify oxygen‐intermediate binding and impede active‐site regeneration if their polarized coordination environments are not properly regulated. Herein, a metal‐core‐buffered vacancy‐shell strategy is proposed by coupling ultrasmall metallic Co nanodots with a Co‐vacancy‐rich CoO x /C shell within a conductive mesoporous carbon framework. The metallic Co core serves as a nanoscale electron reservoir, while the vacancy‐rich CoO x /C shell provides adsorption‐regulating Co─O─C motifs for oxygen intermediates. Structural and spectroscopic characterizations confirm the formation of a carbon‐confined Co/CoO x core–shell architecture with abundant vacancy‐related defects. In situ Raman spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that interfacial electronic coupling buffers the vacancy‐induced polarized Co─O─C motifs, downshifts the Co 3d‐band center, and weakens excessive *OH binding, thereby balancing oxygen‐species activation with active‐site regeneration. As a result, Co@v‐CoO x /C delivers a high ORR half‐wave potential of 0.871 V, an OER overpotential of 319 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , and a small bifunctional potential gap of 0.678 V. Rechargeable Zn‐air batteries based on Co@v‐CoO x /C achieve a peak power density of 184 mW cm −2 and stable cycling for approximately 3200 h, while flexible devices also show high power output and mechanical tolerance.

title: One‐Step Synthesis of Supramolecular Nanoparticles With Interlocking‐Enhanced Two‐Photon Fluorescence
abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional organic two‐photon excited fluorescence (TPEF) materials relying on extended π ‐conjugated backbones inherently suffer from complex synthesis, limited biocompatibility, and aggregation‐caused quenching (ACQ). In this work, conceptually inspired by the interlocking design in engineering structures, we develop a facile one‐step supramolecular assembly strategy to fabricate poly(2,5‐diamino‐1,4‐benzenedithiol) (PMBT) supramolecular nanoparticles (SNPs). The SNPs are constructed through the synergistic interplay of disulfide polymerization, hydrogen bonding, and π – π stacking, resulting in an interlocking‐enhanced, short‐range locally ordered structure that lacks extended π ‐conjugated backbones. The interlocking architecture not only effectively suppresses nonradiative decay pathways by restricting molecular motion within the rigidified matrix, but also facilitates efficient exciton coupling and radiative recombination through enhanced interchain electronic communication. Consequently, PMBT SNPs exhibit favorable overall performance, including high aqueous stability, favorable fluorescence properties (quantum yield of 9% ± 1%, lifetime of 15.6 ns), exceptional two‐photon absorption cross‐section of up to 6.3 × 10 5 GM at 800 nm excitation, favorable biocompatibility (>85% cell viability at 200 µg/mL for 48 h), and deep‐tissue imaging capabilities. This work establishes a supramolecular engineering paradigm that harnesses intermolecular interactions, thereby enabling the development of high‐performance two‐photon clusterization‐triggered emissive materials.

title: Dynamically Tunable Near‐Infrared Photoluminescence with Long‐Wavelength Energy Transfer Engineered by Multilevel Supramolecular Confinement
abstract: One of the major challenges in fabricating advanced optical materials is the achievement of efficient and tunable emission in the red to near-infrared range. To address this critical issue, a multilevel confinement strategy is employed to construct a supramolecular photoswitch, which is initially achieved by the formation of a unique 2:2 host-guest complex between cucurbit[8]uril and biphenyl-conjugated bipyridinium salt, followed by the intermolecular electrostatic wrapping with the negatively charged β-cyclodextrin-grafted hyaluronic acid. This two-stage assembling process can significantly immobilize the molecular conformation and potentiate the photoluminescence emission of the bipyridinium guest to ultimately induce a 40-fold enhancement of the red emission at 650 nm. The cyclodextrin units on the polysaccharide skeleton can further encapsulate adamantane-modified diarylethene, conferring the desired photoswitchable properties to the supramolecular assembly. The fluorescence emission can be reversibly regulated with a high photo-switching ratio and excellent fatigue resistance. Remarkably, near-infrared emission at 790 nm can be further achieved via Förster resonance energy transfer to Cy7. Benefiting from its photoswitching properties, the system is successfully applied in anti-counterfeiting and information encryption. This study establishes a versatile supramolecular engineering paradigm for constructing tunable red-to-near-infrared emission systems, which may open new avenues for designing dynamic optical and information encryption materials.

title: Guest-Programmed Adaptive Redistribution in Heteroleptic Metal–Organic Cages
abstract: Abstract Adaptive reconfiguration of complex supramolecular assemblies remains a fundamental challenge in synthetic chemistry, especially for heteroleptic systems prone to kinetic traps and component scrambling. Here, we report a guest-coupled reassembly strategy that enables programmable redistribution between cage architectures in heteroleptic pentagonal prismatic ZnII cages, assembled via precise edge-length matching between pentatopic and tetratopic ligands. Distinct from conventional single-guest templation, these cages exhibit adaptive redistribution behavior in which multiguest recognition is coupled to host redistribution within confined cavities. Chlorinated guests are selectively encapsulated through Cl···π and π···π interactions, thereby biasing the thermodynamic landscape of assembly. Secondary guests redirect the assembly equilibrium toward distinct product distributions, including guest release, guest exchange, or stoichiometry-dependent formation of species assigned as a homoleptic pseudo-cubic cage with one or two encapsulated guests. Crystallographic, Hirshfeld surface, and computational analyses reveal that multiple Cl···π, π···π, and C–H···π noncovalent interactions within the confined cavity contribute to the selectivity of guest-directed assembly redistribution. Furthermore, the incorporation of peripheral pyrene units imparts the prismatic cages with photoluminescence, which is enhanced upon guest binding due to framework rigidification. This work demonstrates how confined multiguest recognition can be coupled to compositional redistribution within complex heteroleptic assemblies, providing a foundation for programmable adaptive supramolecular systems.

title: Intermediate Phase Selectivity in ZSM-5 Zeolite Synthesis and Framework Aluminum Distribution
abstract: Abstract The current understanding of zeolite crystallization is still far from well understood. Herein, we show that the crystallization pathway of high-silica ZSM-5, one of the most industrially important zeolites, can be altered not only by the type of organic structure-directing agents (OSDAs) at a gel Si/Al ratio of 50 but also by the simultaneous use of Na+ and Cs+ ions as inorganic structure-directing agents (ISDAs). The use of the diquaternary OSDA 1,8-bis(N-methylpyrrolidinium)octane (1,8-MPO) instead of tetrapropylammonium (TPA), the most common OSDA for the synthesis of ZSM-5, in the presence of Na+ led to zeolite β as an intermediate phase; otherwise, no crystalline intermediate was observed. Also, the addition of a small amount of Cs+ ions (gel Cs/Na = 0.14) as a secondary ISDA to the 1,8-MPO-Na+ and TPA-Na+ systems gave small-pore zeolites bikitaite and analcime as an intermediate phase during synthesis, respectively. More importantly, we found that the framework Al distribution in the final product ZSM-5 could differ according to the in situ transformation pathway of intermediate phases, as well as to the type of OSDA used. This study provides a new strategy for directly controlling the intrazeolitic location of Brønsted acid sites, as well as the nucleation pathway in the synthesis of high-silica zeolites.

title: Decoction-inspired thermo-mechanical coupling creates hierarchical nanohelix from herbal medicine for lipophagy therapy
abstract: Abstract Oral supramolecular nanomedicines often suffer from kinetic trapping, forming metastable aggregates with poor gastrointestinal stability and premature drug release. Conventional assembly methods rarely overcome these barriers. Inspired by the traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) decoction process, which intrinsically combines heating with mechanical stirring, we applied a thermo-mechanical coupling strategy to baicalin and berberine assemblies. Coupled thermal energy and fluid shear drove a transition from kinetically trapped metastable aggregate to thermodynamically stable left-handed nanohelix with an ordered crystalline lattice. This higher degree of structural order conferred improved gastrointestinal tolerance and extended the in vivo mean residence time to 23.06 ± 0.47 h. Sustained systemic exposure activated the AMPK–FoxO1–TFEB–lysosome axis, promoted hepatic lipophagy, and alleviated metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease in mice. These findings provide a physical chemistry framework for overcoming kinetic traps in supramolecular assembly, elucidate the nanoscale organization underlying traditional decoction, and offer a design strategy for long-acting oral nanotherapeutics.

title: Topology-Directed Pore Space Compartmentalization and Densification in MOFs Enable Record Trace C3H6 Capture and C2H4 Purification
abstract: Abstract Adsorptive separation of C3H6 from C2H4 is of great relevance yet highly challenging to the petrochemical industry, especially for trace C3H6 capture. Here, we constructed two metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), NKU-410 and NKU-411, through pillaring of the kgd- and hxl-topology supermolecular building layers (SBLs) comprised of a novel fluoride-bridging hexanuclear niccolite cluster. In terms of topological net merging and pillaring, a three-dimensional compartmentalization of pore space was implemented, reconstructing the less confined pore space in NKU-410 into a dense array of uniform strongly confined pore cavities in NKU-411. Leveraging the pore confinement effect, NKU-411 impressively attains an ultrahigh C3H6 uptake of 47.5 cm3 g–1 at 298 K and 0.01 bar, together with an appreciable C3H6/C2H4 (1/99, v/v) selectivity of 36.9, placing it among the benchmark MOFs for trace C3H6 capture from C2H4. Dynamic breakthrough experiments demonstrated that NKU-411 shows excellent C2H4 purification and C3H6 recovery performances at ambient conditions over a wide range of separation scenarios with varying feed concentrations and compositions, remarkably affording a record-breaking C2H4 (≥99.999% pure) productivity of 639.4 L kg–1 from C3H6/C2H4 (1/99, v/v) mixture. In-depth mechanistic studies disclosed that the well-tailored pore cavity in NKU-411 represents a “sweet spot” for C3H6 and the dense arrangement of such “sweet spot” maximally optimizes the pore space utilization, providing a new paradigm for boosting the ultralow-pressure gas adsorption capacity and selectivity for MOFs.

title: Diffusion-Gating Enabled Ternary C2H4 Purification and Inverse C2H2/CO2 Separation in an Adaptive Hopf-Link Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract The simultaneous purification of polymer-grade ethylene (C2H4) and recovery of high-purity acetylene (C2H2) from complex ternary mixtures with carbon dioxide (CO2) represents a critical industrial challenge. Conventional adsorbents employ thermodynamic selectivity to bind C2H2 and CO2 preferentially over C2H4, enabling one-step C2H4 purification but necessitating an energy-intensive desorption step for C2H2 recovery, as C2H2 typically binds more strongly. Here, we report a fundamentally different approach using diffusion-gating in an adaptive Hopf-link metal–organic framework, ZJNU-600, which replaces thermodynamic control. The framework comprises two orthogonal, interpenetrated sql nets mechanically interlocked as Hopf links, with thiocyanate linkers acting as molecular hinges that modulate the pore aperture. This architecture establishes an ideal kinetic diffusion hierarchy of CO2 &gt; C2H2 &gt; C2H4, completely inverting the elution order compared to equilibrium-based separation. Dynamic breakthrough experiments demonstrate that ZJNU-600 achieves one-step production of C2H4 from ternary mixtures while simultaneously enabling the direct recovery of C2H2 via inverse separation, eliminating the need for energy-intensive desorption. The exceptionally low isosteric heat of CO2 adsorption (24.7 kJ mol–1) further suggests minimal regeneration energy. Computational studies reveal that the diffusion barrier hierarchy arises from the differential chemical compatibility of each gas with the hydroxyl-decorated pore walls. This work establishes kinetic pore-aperture engineering as a generalizable and energy-efficient design principle for multicomponent gas separations, effectively inverting the separation hierarchy dictated by thermodynamic affinity.

title: Framework Deuteration Regulates Excited-State Dynamics and H2O2 Release in Covalent Organic Framework Photocatalysis
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen/deuterium (H/D) substitution provides a unique means of perturbing nuclear motion while largely preserving electronic structure. Here, we investigate isotope-regulated photocatalysis using structurally matched H-TpPa and D-TpPa covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for H2O2 production. Deuteration preserves framework connectivity, crystallinity, porosity, and ground-state electronic structure, yet increases the H2O2 production rate by 1.80-fold in O2-saturated pure water. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses show that D-TpPa exhibits weaker effective exciton–phonon coupling, a lower apparent exciton-dissociation energy, a longer-lived photoexcited population, and redistributed mode-resolved Huang–Rhys contributions, collectively improving charge utilization. Both isotopologues follow the same coupled two-electron oxygen reduction and four-electron water oxidation pathway. At the catalytic interface, isotope-dependent vibrational free-energy contributions reduce terminal *HOOH stabilization and lower the free-energy requirement for H2O2 release. These results establish framework isotope engineering as a generic strategy for regulating photocatalysis from excited-state evolution to interfacial product release without substantial electronic reconstruction.

title: Conjugation of metal-organic framework (MIL-125) to NiFe2O4@CdS nanoparticles for enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen generation
abstract: Abstract Harnessing solar energy with semiconductors offers a feasible path toward sustainable hydrogen production via photocatalytic water splitting. In this study, a ternary photocatalyst, MIL-125(Ti)/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS, was fabricated by integrating a Ti-based metal–organic framework with a green-synthesized NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS binary core–shell heterostructure for visible-light-driven hydrogen evolution. Illicium verum Hook. f. (star anise) extract was used as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent for NiFe 2 O 4 nanoparticles preparation prior to the fabrication of the binary photocatalyst. The ternary composite was comprehensively characterized by structural, morphological, optical, and photoelectrochemical techniques. Compared with the individual components, the ternary photocatalyst exhibited enhanced visible-light absorption, a reduced band gap (2.42 eV), and a mesoporous structure with a BET surface area of 148.62 m²/g, pore volume of 0.5721 cm 3 /g, and a mean pore diameter of 15.0 nm. Photoelectrochemical analyses revealed improved charge separation, the lowest charge-transfer resistance, the highest photocurrent response, the largest electrochemically active surface area, and favorable band alignment. Consequently, MIL-125/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS achieved an initial hydrogen evolution rate of 1.62231 mmol g − 1 h − 1 and a cumulative hydrogen production of 10.20386 mmol g − 1 after 5 h, significantly outperforming CdS and the binary NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS. The photocatalyst retained approximately 60% of its initial activity after four reaction cycles, demonstrating good stability. The enhanced performance is attributed to the synergistic effects of MIL-125, which increase surface area, improve light harvesting, and promote efficient charge separation and transfer through a dual direct Z-scheme heterojunction. These findings highlight MIL-125/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS as a promising photocatalyst for sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Bio-Assisted Self-Activation of Porous Carbon in the Presence of Endogenous Silica for High-Performance Supercapacitors
abstract: Abstract In the pursuit of high-performance supercapacitors, it remains a key challenge to rationally engineer carbon electrodes with concurrently optimized porosity, surface chemistry, and structural integrity. In this work, a plant-mediated self-activation strategy is developed to construct hierarchically porous and nitrogen-doped carbon materials via endogenous nanosilica uptake. During plant growth, uniformly distributed SiO2 acts as both an in situ hard template and a catalytic promoter during carbonization, enabling the formation of a hierarchical pore structure without external activation. Meanwhile, SiO2-regulated nitrogen metabolism induces intrinsic nitrogen doping in the derived carbon framework, establishing a coupled biological-chemical pathway for heteroatom incorporation. The optimized SiO2-100@C delivers a high specific capacitance of 259.3 F g–1 at 0.5 A g–1 and retains 85% at 5.0 A g–1, together with excellent cycling stability of 95.53% after 20,000 cycles. The superior performance is attributed to synergistic effects of hierarchical porosity, enhanced ion transport, and regulated heteroatom configuration within a robust C-SiO2-derived framework. This work provides a sustainable and scalable strategy that integrates biological uptake with nanoscale structural engineering for advanced carbon-based energy storage materials.

title: Programming Closed Pores in Hard Carbon Anodes via Alcohol‐Regulated Interfacial Assembly for High‐Rate and Durable Sodium‐Ion Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Closed pores are widely recognized as the primary structural domains responsible for the low‐voltage plateau capacity of hard carbon anodes for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, current strategies for constructing closed pores predominantly rely on post‐carbonization reconstruction, offering limited control over pore accessibility and interfacial chemistry. Here we demonstrate that closed pores can instead be programmed during the precursor assembly process via an alcohol‐regulated interfacial assembly strategy. By systematically modulating the alcohol/water solvent environment, hydrogen‐bond interactions, micelle swelling behavior, and pyrrole polymerization kinetics are cooperatively regulated, enabling programmable precursor confinement and the subsequent transformation of micelle‐pyrrole assemblies into closed‐pore‐rich hard carbons during carbonization. The optimized hard carbon exhibits abundant closed ultramicropores that not only facilitate the quasi‐metallic sodium cluster filling but also promote the formation of a thin inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer, thereby accelerating sodium‐storage kinetics. As a result, it delivers an outstanding rate capability of 119 mAh g −1 at 10 A g −1 and robust cycling stability over 6000 cycles at 5 A g −1 , as well as excellent low‐temperature performance at −20°C. This work establishes precursor organization programming as a general strategy for constructing closed pores in hard carbon materials toward fast‐charging and long‐life SIBs.

title: Blending With Insulating Polymers Enables Stable Anti‐Ambipolar Characteristics in n‐Type Organic Mixed‐Conductors for Heterogeneous Spiking Neurons
abstract: ABSTRACT Mammalian neurons exhibit diverse structural and physiological properties: a heterogeneity not present in current neuromorphic systems. Recent advancements have led to bio‐realistic spiking systems which are based on the integration and long‐term operation of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) with anti‐ambipolar characteristics. However, the library of materials enabling anti‐ambipolarity (AA) is restricted by the lack of stable, fast, and scalable organic mixed ionic and electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibiting this specific OFF‐ON‐OFF behavior. This complicates mimicking specialized neuron types. Blending semiconducting with insulating polymers is a classic organic and OMIEC electronics strategy to improve device performance and enable tunability, yet unexplored for improving anti‐ambipolar stability in non‐ladder‐type anti‐ambipolar materials. Here, the n‐type OMIEC, P(gNDI‐gT2), is blended with the insulating polymer, PMMA, yielding stable anti‐ambipolar characteristics. The miscibility in solution forms a mechanically stabilizing and ion‐permeable framework in the solid state that considerably reduces swelling‐induced structural damage, thus preventing dramatic failure after the first operation cycles without compromising the conductive polymer's electronic pathways. Modulating the polymer blend ratio enables low‐power, fast‐spiking Hodgkin–Huxley neurons with tunable and programmable dynamics, without optimized device geometries, demonstrating frequency deconvolution and reservoir computing. These two computing primitive building blocks are essential for designing efficient spiking neural networks.

title: Crystal Integrity Suppresses Bulk Trapping in Potassium Poly(Heptazine Imide) for Selective Polyester Photoreforming
abstract: ABSTRACT Bulk defects in organic semiconductor photocatalysts intercept photogenerated charges before interfacial reaction, constraining activity and selectivity. Here, seeded molten‐salt recrystallization yields potassium poly(heptazine imide) (PHI‐K) nanocrystals with reduced cyano content and enhanced lattice coherence for polyester photoreforming. Density functional theory and transient absorption spectroscopy identify cyano‐derived occupied states as bulk hole traps. Defect suppression preserves observable hole‐polaron absorption and extends the average exciton‐associated absorption decay time from 69.52 to 984.72 ps, consistent with reduced trap‐assisted carrier loss. Under air mass 1.5 global (AM 1.5G) irradiation, crystalline PHI‐K photoreforms alkaline‐pretreated poly(glycolic acid) and poly(lactic acid) into glyoxylic and pyruvic acids with respective target‐product carbon yields of 95.2% and 92.5%. Corresponding H 2 evolution rates reach 42.6 and 26.0 mmol g −1 h −1 , with apparent quantum yields of 50.8% and 30.1% at 400 nm, respectively. In situ infrared spectroscopy, isotope effects, and carrier kinetics support a pathway in which holes drive two‐electron oxidation of surface‐bound α‐hydroxy species while electrons reduce protons on Pt. These findings establish crystal integrity as an organic semiconductor materials principle that couples bulk charge retention to selective bond conversion in conjugated photocatalysts.

title: Supramolecular Assembly‐Driven Photofluorochromism Enables Time‐Encoded Transient Encryption
abstract: ABSTRACT Stimuli‐responsive luminescent materials offer dynamic optical outputs for advanced information security, yet achieving programmable fluorescence color evolution in water using a single optical input remains challenging. We developed a water‐soluble zwitterionic monomer, 2‐(pent‐4‐en‐1‐yl)isoquinolin‐2‐ium‐5‐sulfonate (IQIS), that exhibits pronounced photofluorochromism under ultraviolet (UV) irradiation. Its fluorescence evolves from blue to green, accompanied by an increase in the overall fluorescence quantum yield from 3.5% to 17.3%. Mechanistic studies reveal that IQIS is weakly pre‐associated in water, while UV irradiation promotes the growth, densification, and packing reorganization of these loose molecular clusters. The resulting long‐wavelength emission exhibits distinct aggregation‐dependent photophysical characteristics and is consistent with an aggregate‐associated excited state with enhanced intermolecular charge‐transfer character. By programming the kinetics of this supramolecular reorganization in different polymeric architectures, high‐resolution grayscale patterns with time‐evolving optical outputs can be generated. Under continuous UV irradiation, the same light used for fluorescence readout simultaneously drives the optical evolution, causing initially visible information to progressively fade and ultimately disappear without an additional stimulus. This single‐input, self‐evolving behavior enables a “Snapchat‐like” transient encryption mode and provides a strategy for spatiotemporal information encoding based on kinetically programmed supramolecular photofluorochromism.

title: Particle-Mediated Tuning of Defect Stability in Lamellar Block Copolymer Systems
abstract: Abstract We study how colloidal inclusions modify the formation energy of dislocation pairs in lamellar block copolymer systems. Using a hybrid particle/Ginzburg–Landau model, we calculate defect formation energies by comparing defect-free and defect-containing states with and without embedded colloids. Finite-size scaling is used to obtain formation energies in the thermodynamic limit. The effect of colloid insertion depends strongly on particle sizes and surface patterning. Homogeneous particles increasingly stabilize dislocation pairs with increasing particle sizes. Particles larger than one lamellar domain preferentially occupy the dislocation cores, where they replace strained polymer rather than deforming defect-free lamellae. The magnitude of this stabilization depends on surface affinity. Balanced Janus particles instead increase the formation energy, because their competing surface preferences cannot be satisfied simultaneously near the curved core. Varying the patch ratio interpolates between these limits. Surface patterning has little effect for particles smaller than one lamellar domain, but changes the formation energy by several tens of reduced energy units (roughly 10–40 kBT for typical block copolymers) for larger particles. These results provide quantitative guidelines for controlling topological defect stability in lamellar block copolymer systems.

title: ATP-dependent dimerization of BrxC coordinates BrxBCZ assembly for phage exclusion
abstract: Abstract Bacteriophage Exclusion (BREX) systems protect bacterial genomes via sequence-specific DNA methylation while blocking phage replication through a poorly understood “restriction-without-cleavage” mechanism. Here, we present cryo-EM structures and functional characterization of the core BREX machinery from Escherichia coli . We determined the structures of the ATPase BrxC in its monomeric state and two ATPγS-bound dimeric conformations, showing that ATP binding, not hydrolysis, triggers dimerization. The conserved Arg328 couples dimer formation to ATP hydrolysis and is required for both phage restriction and host methylation; the R328A mutant supports assembly but abolishes defense. We further resolved the BrxBCZ ternary complex, revealing BrxB as a central scaffold bridging the BrxC dimer and BrxZ without direct BrxC–BrxZ contact. Biochemical assays show that BrxZ is a dual-function enzyme with alkaline phosphatase and metal-dependent nuclease activities. Thus, ATP drives BrxC assembly and inhibits BrxZ activities. Disruption of the BrxB–BrxC interface or the BrxC ATPase cycle selectively eliminates restriction while preserving methylation, establishing BrxBCZ as a restriction-specific structural core. Collectively, these findings delineate the structural basis for ATP-dependent coordination of BREX, revealing how energy metabolism is integrated into bacterial innate immunity.

title: Modular Biofabrication of Functional Skeletal Muscle Incorporated with Endothelialized Microvascular Seed‐Derived Lumenized Microvessels
abstract: The clinical translation of engineered skeletal muscle (eSM) for volumetric muscle regeneration is hindered by the challenge of establishing a functional vascular network capable of sustaining its high metabolic demand and ensuring graft survival. Here, we present a bottom-up biofabrication strategy to generate a pre-vascularized in vitro eSM model through the modular assembly of independently matured muscle and vascular compartments. C2C12 myoblasts were encapsulated within core-shell fibers using rotary wet-spinning (RoWS), yielding anisotropically aligned, multinucleated, and contractile myofibers expressing myosin heavy chain and sarcomeric α-actinin. In parallel, gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)-based microvascular seeds (µVS), pre-endothelialized with human umbilical vein endothelial cells, were engineered to guide rapid and structurally stable vascular formation while preventing uncontrolled capillary self-organization. Fully endothelialized µVS were incorporated into a pro-angiogenic bioink and processed via RoWS to generate tubular vascular fibers with physiological diameters (100-200 µm) and continuous CD31-positive lumens. After independent maturation, muscle and vascular constructs were bioassembled into a hierarchically organized tissue and co-cultured. By decoupling myogenic and angiogenic differentiation, this strategy overcomes medium incompatibility typical of conventional co-cultures, preserving compartment-specific architecture and function and establishing a versatile platform for muscle-vascular modeling and translational muscle repair.

title: Layer-by-layer water filling in molecular-scale capillaries monitored by AFM
abstract: Abstract Under ambient humidity, water spontaneously condenses in pores only a few nanometers in size, making nanoscale capillarity central to numerous natural phenomena and technological applications. At these dimensions, water may no longer be treated as a continuous fluid, yet the consequences of molecular discreteness for capillary condensation and filling remain poorly understood. Here we study two-dimensional (2D) nanocapillaries fabricated by van der Waals assembly and, using atomic force microscopy (AFM), monitor their wall deformations during humidity-driven water uptake. We observe two distinct regimes: layer-by-layer filling of flexible capillaries and abrupt filling of more rigid ones. Flexible walls deform in ≈3 Å steps, consistent with the entry of individual molecular layers of water. The different filling regimes are explained by a competition between wall deformation energy and oscillatory wall-water interactions. These results, together with the theoretical framework developed here, show how molecular discreteness can profoundly affect ubiquitous capillary phenomena, with wall rigidity determining whether this discreteness is exposed or hidden within an apparently classical, Kelvin-like response.

title: When are Two‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks Good Electrodes for Lithium Ion Batteries? A Data‐Driven Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are emerging as sustainable organic electrode candidates for lithium‐ion batteries. Despite more than a decade of research, existing heuristics for designing electroactive COFs lack generality, and the suitability of these materials as alternatives to conventional electrodes remains poorly resolved. Here, we map structure–electrode–function relationships across 1099 experimentally synthesized 2D COFs from the CoRE COF database by developing a data‐driven framework integrating density‐functional theory computations with machine learning models and establishing atomic‐level design rules governing electrode behavior. We uncover that cathode‐like character originates from dense, multidentate nitrogen and oxygen rich coordination pockets at pore walls, characteristic of imide, acylhydrazones, keto–amine linkages, and π‐macrocycles, whereas anode‐like behavior is encoded by spatially separated redox sites and π‐rich interlayer galleries that sustain weak, reversible Li + intercalation. Sequential voltage, capacity, and conductivity‐based screening across the database yields 14 anode and 14 cathode candidates. We show that the known chemical space of 2D COFs cannot outperform inorganic electrodes in terms of operating voltages. However, strategic pairing of 2D anode|cathode pairs within an all‐organic lithium battery architecture delivers full‐cell voltages exceeding 2 V with capacities above 200 mAh g −1 on both electrodes, surpassing small organic molecules and polymer counterparts.

title: Spent Coffee Grounds‐Derived Micro‐Nano‐Architectured Air Filtration Membranes for Multiwavelength Light‐Triggered Bioaerosol Inactivation
abstract: ABSTRACT Indoor air carries particulate matter, toxic gases, and viable microorganisms, yet filtration systems treat them separately at an added energy cost. We introduce a membrane that targets all three by spatially segregating two metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) within a micro‐nanostructured architecture: one for gas adsorption, and the other is positioned at the particle‐capture interface. The membrane is fabricated in a single step by simultaneous electrospinning of MOF‐177‐loaded polyacrylonitrile nanofibers and electrospraying of ZIF‐8‐decorated spent coffee ground (SCG) microparticles. SCG, a waste stream exceeding 10 million tons annually, exhibits multiwavelength photothermal activity via bio‐derived chromophores and develops hydrophobicity upon mild annealing. At 4.5 times the NIOSH respirator test velocity, the membrane captures 99.7% of PM 2.5 at roughly half the pressure drop of an equivalent MOF‐free membrane, while removing 83.4% of ammonia vapor. The membrane reaches above 80°C under simulated sunlight, enabling chemical‐free, external‐power‐free microbial inactivation of accumulated bioaerosols; after 3 days of real office‐air exposure, a single 10 min simulated solar exposure or a 20 min near‐infrared (NIR) exposure restored effective microbial suppression. This establishes a generalizable principle: spatially resolved co‐deposition of multiple functional agents via twin electrohydrodynamic techniques can convert an organic waste stream into a self‐sterilizing air‐purification platform.

title: Bottom-up synthesis of amorphous silica nanosheets
abstract: Amorphous silica nanosheets have recently emerged as a new class of two-dimensional (2D) materials owing to their unique structures and properties that differ significantly from those of bulk amorphous silica. While extensive studies have been conducted on substrate-supported amorphous silica nanosheets prepared by vapor-phase methods, the bottom-up synthesis of free-standing amorphous silica nanosheets in solution remains relatively unexplored. In this review, recent progress in the bottom-up synthesis of amorphous silica nanosheets is summarized, including hard-template approaches, interfacial templating methods, and surfactant-templating strategies. Particular attention is devoted to surfactant-directed synthesis, which has long been investigated as a route to two-dimensional silica structures. The formation mechanisms, structural characteristics, and limitations of conventional liquid-phase surfactant-templated systems are discussed. Furthermore, a recently developed solid-state surfactant templating method is introduced as a new strategy for producing free-standing amorphous silica nanosheets with molecularly controlled thickness. This method enables monolayer exfoliation, sub-nanometer-scale thickness control, and extension to organo-siloxane nanosheets with diverse compositions. The assembly of these nanosheets into densely packed ultrathin films and their potential applications are also described. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for the synthesis, structural analysis, and functional development of amorphous silica nanosheets are discussed.

title: Molecular alloying of titanium–oxo clusters for linker-free S-scheme interfaces
abstract: Abstract Heterojunction engineering is one of the most effective strategies for enhancing charge separation and improving the performance of photo-functional materials. However, such heterojunction functionality has been almost exclusively realized in extended solids, and how to translate this concept into atomically precise molecular systems remains an open question. Here, we employ two isostructural yet electronically distinct titanium-oxo clusters, Ti 12 Mn 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 and Ti 12 Cr 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 (denoted as TiMn and TiCr, respectively; Bz denotes C 6 H 5 CO 2 ), as modular nanosized building blocks to construct molecular alloys that form eutectic molecular alloys across the entire compositional range. Free from covalent or ionic linkages, TiMn and TiCr achieve spontaneous Fermi-level equilibration solely through intimate intermolecular packing, thereby establishing an S-scheme junction at the molecular scale. This markedly enhances charge-carrier separation, carrier lifetime, and interfacial charge-transport kinetics, leading to substantially increased photocurrents, accelerated reactive oxygen species generation, and significantly improved elimination of representative waterborne micropollutants. The emergent functionality originates from local electronic complementarity and low-resistance intermolecular charge-transport channels facilitated by ligand π–π interactions, whereas long-range crystalline order is not essential. Our findings suggest a convenient approach for developing nanocluster-level functional donor–acceptor systems without relying on extended frameworks or on covalent fusion between the building units.

title: In Situ Assembled Carboxyl‐Functionalized Hexaazatrinaphthylene Enables Accelerated Li + Transport and Localized FEC Enrichment in Silicon Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Rational interfacial regulation is critical to resolving the structural instability of high‐performance silicon (Si) anodes for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). Here, a molecular interphase engineering strategy based on hexaazatrinaphthylene tricarboxylic acid (HATNTA), a carboxyl‐functionalized derivative of hexaazatrinaphthylene (HATN), is proposed to regulate the interfacial chemistry of Si anodes. The π‐conjugated framework provides abundant polar nitrogen sites (C═N) that may facilitate Li + coordination. The carboxyl groups incorporated into HATNTA enable localized fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) enrichment, thereby steering the interfacial reaction pathway toward the formation of a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). The resulting interphase suppresses excessive electrolyte decomposition and mitigates electrode swelling and structural degradation during prolonged cycling. The Si‐HATNTA anode achieves an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 92.56%. It exhibits a rate capability of 1122 mAh g −1 at 5 A g −1 and maintains 1341 mAh g −1 after 200 cycles at 1.0 A g −1 . The NCM811//Si‐HATNTA full cell retains 70.49% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles at 0.2 C. This work provides a molecular design strategy for stabilizing Si anodes through interfacial chemistry regulation.

title: Cell Spreading-Enhanced Electron-Transfer Electrochemical Cytosensor Enabling Single-Cell Detection
abstract: Achieving single-cell detection with electrochemical cytosensors remains challenging, owing to a poor understanding of how electroactive redox probes generate measurable signals near large, insulating cells. Here, we validate a cell–electrode interfacial electron-transfer effect, in situ visualizing that the measurable current signal originating from redox probes located at the cell–electrode adjacent interface, rather than from those distributed on the cell surface. Notably, cell spreading enlarges this cell-adjacent interface, thereby enabling effective current amplification. Guided by this effect, we design an integrated cytosensor platform that combines a highly conductive lamellar reduced graphene oxide (RGO)/Ti3C2Tx electrode chip, which facilitates lamellipodia-driven cell spreading, with a high peroxidase-activity FeCN single-atom nanozyme. This platform exhibits a 7.6-fold signal enhancement over conventional chips and a detection limit of 0.03 cells mL−1, allowing a resolvable current response from a single cell on the 2 cm2 large-sized chip. Furthermore, it demonstrates potential feasibility for clinical detection of circulating tumor cells, achieving 96% specificity and 87% sensitivity across 55 blood samples in distinguishing cancer patients from healthy controls. This work establishes a cell spreading-enhanced electron-transfer paradigm and advances electrochemical cytosensing toward high-performance liquid biopsy applications. Electrochemical cytosensors have emerged as powerful tools for single-cell analysis, but generating robust signals from individual cells remains a major challenge. The authors uncover a cell-electrode interfacial electron-transfer effect, in which only redox probes at the cell-electrode interface contribute to measurable currents. Exploiting this mechanism, they develop a cell spreading-enhanced electron-transfer (SEET) cytosensor and apply it to circulating tumor cell detection in 55 patient samples, achieving 96% specificity and 87% sensitivity.

title: Engineering Topological Structures in Nematic Liquid Crystals for Functional Applications
abstract: Abstract Topological structures in nematic liquid crystals (LCs) emerge because of spontaneous symmetry breaking or geometric frustration under specific boundary conditions during the alignment of LC molecules. Historically, these topological structures have been regarded as defects that should be eliminated in the display industry. However, by precisely controlling the topological structures of LCs and utilizing the resulting elastic energy landscapes and physical anisotropy, they can be used not only to model other physical systems but also as functional materials. As a result, the topological structures of LCs have attracted significant attention in condensed matter physics, photonics, and materials science. This Review introduces the underlying principles of topological defects and solitons emerging in nematic and chiral nematic LC systems, comprehensively discussing engineering strategies for their precise manipulation. Building upon these foundations, a broad spectrum of innovative applications, such as colloidal self-assembly, soft actuators, tunable optical and photonic devices, and hardware security systems, have been highlighted. Finally, an outlook is provided for the realization of next-generation functional devices and active metamaterials.

title: Steering directional charge migration via ordered self-assembled molecular layers for efficient BiVO4-silicon artificial leaf
abstract: Abstract The BiVO 4 -silicon artificial leaf represents a promising unbiased photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting device, yet its efficiency remains limited by sluggish charge transport in the BiVO 4 photoanode. To overcome these limitations, we propose a self-assembled molecular-bridge strategy to establish ordered and fast pathways for efficient charge transport between BiVO 4 and NiFeCoO x oxygen evolution cocatalysts (OECs). To clarify the role of dipole strength, we compare two self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) with distinct dipole moments: [4-(9H-carbazol-9-yl)ethyl]phosphonic acid (4PACZ ~ 1.83 Debye) and (4-(7H-dibenzo[c,g]carbazol-7-yl)butyl)phosphonic acid (4PADCB ~ 2.54 Debye). The larger dipole of 4PADCB generates a stronger interfacial electric field (IEF), which drives directional hole extraction and suppresses recombination. Consequently, the optimized BiVO 4 /4PADCB/NiFeCoO x photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.35 mA cm⁻ 2 at 1.23 V versus a reversible hydrogen electrode (V RHE ), ranking among the best BiVO 4 -based systems modified with organic interfacial layers. Furthermore, by integrating the photoanode with a silicon solar cell, a standalone artificial leaf (1.5 cm 2 area) was constructed, achieving a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 8.75% and stable operation for over 15 hours. This work establishes a clear link between molecular dipole strength and interfacial charge separation, providing a generalizable design principle for molecular interface engineering in PEC water splitting.
